title: Commuting integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs revisited: certified densities, spectral rigidity, and an exact identification at the c=1 branch point
comment: 28 pages. Single consolidated article, per the moderators' invitation (MOD-101633), merging submissions submit/7974478 and submit/7974538
summary: We revisit the commuting local integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs constructed in hep-th/0404195 as input data for integrable boundary states, using exact-arithmetic operator-product engines. A bootstrap lemma reduces its overdetermined bilinear commutativity systems to a distinguished odd charge D plus linear kernel problems -- conditionally on even-spin vacancy, a machine-verified but finite-range input. For the Z_2 x Z_2 "paperclip" family we publish the spin-7 density P_8, prove [I_3,I_5]=[I_3,I_7]=[I_5,I_7]=0 identically in n, and verify the Lukyanov-Vitchev-Zamolodchikov four-screening characterization at spins 7 and 9 at sampled n. For the A_2^(2) family we give an exact Coulomb-gas dictionary to the dual Phi_{1,2}/Phi_{2,1} perturbations (that identification itself being classical, Zamolodchikov; Smirnov), whence the infinite hierarchy at all spins 6n+-1 follows by the Feigin-Frenkel affine-Toda theorem; our contribution is the certified dictionary, not a new all-spin construction. At c=1 the tower's defining charges are exactly quantum KdV at c_{1,4}=-25/2 -- the all-odd sector of the Freeman-Hornfeck-West family: the hierarchy embeds at every odd spin, equality verified through spin 15, all-spin multiplicity one open. We exclude or disfavor the named non-KdV candidates at the tested loci and identify the self-dual degeneracy as L(1,0). Through spin 11, the generic centralizer of I_3 is, for all three Z_2 x O(N) "cylindrical" families, one-dimensional at odd and zero at even spins, with Q(t)-symbolic charges at spins 7, 9, 11 and an explained fiber jump at N=-2. We certify the published 2004 low-spin formulas and record five corrections (one presumed). All-spin statements are made only where proved, finite-range otherwise. We close with a corank-character conjecture linking the rank deficiencies of the bilinear systems to characters of screening kernels.

title: Exact Solutions to Matrix Models and String Theories: The Global Construction
comment: 190 pages, 68 figures, 3 tables, 4 appendices; 85 plot files, jheppub-nosort.sty
summary: Exact nonperturbative solutions to matrix models and string theories are obtained in closed-form via a discrete-Fourier/Zak-transform representation of their partition-function resurgent-transseries. Examples include all hermitian one-matrix models (paired with their topological string duals) alongside all their multicritical and minimal-string double-scaling limits. The resulting structure is resonant, necessarily including both eigenvalues (D-branes) and anti-eigenvalues (negative-tension-branes). In a complementary preceding paper these solutions were extensively verified at the local level. In order to study them globally across their phase diagrams, complete non-linear Stokes data (and corresponding connection formulae) are still needed -- all of which are obtained herein. This involves a careful study of (anti-) eigenvalue tunneling across the complete multi-sheeted structure of their associated spectral-curves, and how the result descends from multi-cut smooth-curves to single-cut singular-curves -- all of which are extensively checked via large-order analysis and matrix-integral computations. Making use of the resulting exact Stokes automorphisms, nonperturbative solutions can be fully tested, from weak-to-strong 't Hooft coupling, as well as from large-to-small N, and for any complex-values of all parameters, by correctly implementing Stokes-transitions at the crossing of all possible Stokes-lines. Several analytical and numerical tests are carried through in diverse examples covering from matrix models through non-critical strings, which produce very sharp numerical matches fully validating our exact analytical expressions. Anti-eigenvalues or negative-tension D-branes are an absolutely essential part of the story in order to find such precise agreements.

title: Localizing the M-Theory Path Integral: Membrane Instantons
summary: We propose a formula for M2-instanton contributions to the M-theory path integral, incorporating quantum corrections to all orders in the Planck length. The M2-brane action is determined by relative equivariant localization, while an equivariant Dolbeault character computes the one-loop determinant. Continuous families of M2-branes are treated by equivariant localization on their moduli spaces. For M-theory backgrounds dual to ABJM theory, we compute single instanton contributions from linear holomorphic fillings to the sphere partition function and the topologically twisted index associated with supersymmetric $AdS_4$ black holes. Our results reproduce known field theory instanton coefficients and give new analytic predictions for mass and squashing deformations at all Chern-Simons levels. For the $V^{5,2}$ theory, we compute new instanton contributions and establish an exact relation between its partition function at special squashing and that of ABJM theory on the round three-sphere.

title: A Positive Metric on Four-Dimensional QFTs
summary: A natural metric on the space of four-dimensional quantum field theories was introduced by Jack and Osborn in classic work on the local renormalization group. In perturbation theory, the Jack-Osborn metric determines the flow of the $a$-anomaly, and positivity implies the $a$-theorem. We derive a non-perturbative generalization of the Jack-Osborn metric and show that it is non-negative by the averaged null energy condition (ANEC). Consequently, the ANEC implies the strong $a$-theorem, and provides the monotonic function along the flow. The method is based on spectral analysis of the three-point function $\langle \mathcal{O}_I \mathcal{E} \mathcal{O}_J\rangle$, where the $\mathcal{O}_I$ are relevant operators and $\mathcal{E}$ is the averaged null energy. This three-point function is decomposed under the spectrum of null rotations that fix the light ray, leading to a positivity condition at each impact parameter.

title: Layer-dependent $s^{\pm}$ superconducting pairing and influence of incipient bands in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ thin films on real LaSrAlO$_4$ substrate
summary: Motivated by recent advances in ambient-pressure superconducting La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ (LNO) thin films, we theoretically investigate these films by explicitly incorporating the realistic LaSrAlO$_4$ (LSAO) substrate. The Fermi-surface topology of the nickelate thin film closely resembles that of the high-pressure bulk phase, with similar $α$ and $β$ sheets and a small hole-like $γ$ pocket originating from the surface bilayer (BL3). The bonding $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ state of the interfacial bilayer (BL1, adjacent to the LSAO substrate) lies only $\sim 5$ meV below the Fermi level, giving rise to an incipient $γ$ band, while for the middle bilayer (BL2) its energy is much lower ($\sim 95$ meV). Remarkably, no significant spontaneous charge transfer from the LSAO substrate to the LNO film is found. Instead, {\it symmetry-allowed charge disproportionation} occurs between the BLs, with hole doping in BL3 and electron doping in BL1 and BL2. Via the weak-coupling Random Phase Approximation, we find a strong $s^{\pm}$-wave superconducting pairing instability in BL3, while $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $s^{\pm}$ are nearly degenerate in the other bilayers BL1 and BL2. Including the incipient $γ$ band via the Dynamical Cluster Approximation beyond weak coupling, robust $s^{\pm}$-wave pairing is observed in all three layers

title: Formalizing local gauge freedom via bi-equivariant groupoid algebras
summary: Gauge degrees of freedom appear in many different contexts. Here, we describe their emergence in the context of architected metamaterials built from self-coupling blocks with internal symmetries. Quantifying the dynamics requires choices of local frames and the many available options constitute the local gauge degrees of freedom of the problem. In the absence of internal symmetries, the dynamical matrices generating the dynamics are all built from the left regular representation of a groupoid C*-algebra canonically associated to the architecture. If the resonators display internal symmetries, we show that the mentioned groupoid C*-algebra accepts a natural 2-action by the group of internal symmetries and that the local gauge freedom can be encoded in a bi-equivariant sub-groupoid algebra generated from the mentioned 2-action. The latter is shown to be the smallest C*-algebra containing all dynamical matrices that can be engineered in a laboratory, for a given architecture and discrete group of internal symmetries.

title: Analytical Interacting Tight-binding Model for Fractional Chern Insulators
summary: We construct a two-dimensional 2-band tight-binding model with two-body interactions and without magnetic lattice translation, in which both the hopping and interaction are exponentially local (with Gaussian decay) in real space. The interaction is built from pair annihilation operators whose coefficients are hopping amplitudes divided by positive powers of relative distance. Without any band projection, the ground states at $1/3$ filling are exactly fractional Chern insulator (FCI) states (and thus have nonzero gap) for any finite lattice size with any periodic/twist boundary conditions. The FCI ground states are analogous to the discretized version of the Laughlin-like states in the continuum Chern-ideal band, though our FCI states do not require the onsite spinor structure that is necessary in the continuum. We further show analytically that, after adding one unit cell while keeping electron number fixed, the anyonic one-quasihole states are zero-energy ground states of the full Hamiltonian for any finite system size and any quasihole position, analogous to Laughlin quasiholes under the Haldane $V_1$ pseudopotential. Numerical evidence is provided for the possible nonzero gap of the FCI states at $1/3$ filling in the thermodynamic limit, when interaction strength is much smaller than the single-particle band gap.

title: Nonlinear optical response with relaxation in the velocity gauge
summary: We develop a framework for the evaluation of the nonlinear optical conductivity of electrons in crystals, driven by homogeneous optical fields, taking into account dissipation effects within the relaxation time approximation (RTA). The present formalism is based on Hamiltonians with minimal light-matter coupling within the velocity gauge, where the electric field is expressed in terms of a vector potential. The nonlinear conductivities are obtained by perturbatively solving the equation of motion for the single-particle reduced density matrix, which includes dissipative effects via the relaxation time approximation. We present a perturbative method to evaluate the reference equilibrium density matrix, towards which dissipation relaxes the system, which in the velocity gauge adiabatically follows the applied vector potential, and is also broadened by dissipative effects. Comparing with previous formulations based on the length gauge, the present approach has the benefit of avoiding the cumbersome evaluation of derivatives of Bloch states with respect to momentum. We test the presented method against length-gauge results, and calculate second- and third-order responses in a graphene-like tight-binding model with a staggered sublattice potential and a periodic modulation. We find that the relaxation time approximation gives results that deviate both quantitatively and qualitatively from the simple inclusion of an imaginary damping term in the frequencies, referred to as adiabatic switching. At equal relaxation parameter, the leading above-gap injection contribution differs by a factor of two; below the gap, the numerical results indicate a finite imaginary dc response in the small-relaxation limit of the relaxation-time calculation. These results show that adiabatic switching does not generally reproduce relaxation through the equation of motion, even in the small-relaxation limit.

title: Topological signatures of criticality: the Ising case
comment: 22 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to Physical Review E
summary: Topological properties of microscopic configurations may provide additional insight into phase transitions beyond conventional thermodynamic observables. We investigate this idea in the two-dimensional Ising model on square and triangular lattices by associating cell complexes with the positive and negative spin domains and constructing an Euler-characteristic observable from their difference. We provide the expression relating this quantity to conventional observables of the Ising model. This derivation allows us to understand its expected behavior physically. As a byproduct, we show that at any finite positive temperature the expectation of the Euler characteristic exceeds a positive, lattice-size-independent bound, hence disproving a previously suggested conjecture. Monte Carlo simulations combined with multihistogram reweighting show that this spin-odd topological observable exhibits order-parameter-like behavior near the ferromagnetic transition. Finite-size scaling of its susceptibility yields pseudocritical temperatures that converge to the known critical temperature for both lattice geometries. On the square lattice, the leading-order estimate of the critical exponent obtained from the topological observable depends more strongly on the fitting range than the magnetization estimate. This behavior is consistent with stronger subleading finite-size corrections, as supported by fits including an additional correction term. On the triangular lattice, the corresponding estimate remains consistent with the theoretical Ising value. Our study suggests that topologically defined quantities such as the Euler characteristic can provide an alternative way to locate order-disorder phase transitions in the systems considered here. Since the definition of these observables is purely geometrical, they can provide useful insights in cases in which order parameters cannot be constructed.

title: Critical--localized reentry under periodic spacer control
summary: Tracking a fixed fraction of a quasiperiodic spectrum tests whether repeated critical--localized alternation extends over a nonzero spectral weight. We find such alternation in a matched-dimer chain by varying only the spacer on-site energies and following a fixed interval of integrated-density-of-states (IDS) labels. An exact Bloch-determinant identity links the physical transfer discriminant to the bands of a periodic reference operator. For the golden cell frequency, we prove that, on a common full-measure set of phases and for every finite value of the spacer control, the physical spectrum in the open reference bands is critical, with purely singular-continuous spectrum and zero Lyapunov exponent, while the spectrum strictly outside the bands is pure point, with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions. Validated IDS bounds certify repeated critical--localized alternation of the same fixed spectral fraction at successive spacer controls. Spacer shifts move the physical levels and reference-band edges at different rates, allowing us to reshape finite-chain return windows and place their endpoints at prescribed controls. An affine recalibration relocates the control family exactly.

title: Cross-probing van der Waals multiferroics
summary: Multiferroic materials, with coupled electric and magnetic orders, hold the potential to enable low-power memory and logic devices by replacing electrical currents with electric fields for magnetic switching. Reducing the dimensionality of multiferroics, from 3D to 2D, has opened new frontiers in this already burgeoning field by enabling unprecedented control over magnetoelectric coupling that is beyond the reach of bulk counterparts, owing to reduced electrostatic screening and enhanced quantum fluctuations at the atomically thin limit. A notable example is a few-layer NiI2 multiferroic, which exhibits coexisting chiral spin textures and (anti)ferroelectricity, accompanied by strong magnetoelectric coupling; by simultaneously breaking time-reversal and spatial-inversion symmetry, NiI2 shows new physical properties such as unique mutual control of chiral magnetism and polarization with giant magnetoelectric coupling, ultrafast electromagnon excitations and odd-parity p-wave magnetism. However, there are experimental challenges in unambiguously identifying intrinsic multiferroicity. This Review critically examines the current landscape of 2D multiferroic materials, with an emphasis on experimental methodologies rather than material taxonomy. We assess different conventional probes for magnetism and ferroelectricity and identify key limitations in single-technique approaches. We emphasize the importance of magneto-opto-electric cross-correlative measurements in establishing intrinsic multiferroic behaviour and outline future research directions for both fundamental studies and device applications.

title: Horizon kinematics and the fine structure induced by finite-energy Hawking radiation
summary: Hawking radiation can modify the horizon structure of a black hole through the loss of mass and global charges. Investigating this process through quantum tunneling, we develop a systematic strategy to reconstruct horizon displacements under finite-energy emission, even when their radii are not explicitly known. Inversion of the horizon condition allows to follow roots's displacements along sequences of static geometries. As a concrete realization, we consider a nonlinearly charged extension of the Bañados--Teitelboim--Zanelli (BTZ) family, whose horizon structure offers an ideal setup to explore this process. Of particular interest is an initial configuration with a double inner horizon coexisting with a simple event horizon. We show that neutral emission necessarily splits the inner root into two simple ones, revealing a horizon fine structure. For charged emission, the dependence of extracted charge on emitted energy determines the separation law and allows that preservation or later restore the degeneracy. We construct such channels connecting the same initial and final states through distinct internal histories sharing the same leading semiclassical factor. As emission continues, the larger of the newly separated inner horizons can coalesce with the event horizon, driving the sequence towards extremality with a vanishing temperature but finite tunneling probability. We find that zero temperature cannot be attained in finite boundary time while uniform adiabaticity bounds hold. We also establish a regime where the geometric expansion and the canonical thermal approximation remain controlled near this endpoint. Finally, applying this analysis to the sector reproducing a quantum-backreacted BTZ geometry reveals how the leading semiclassical corrections raise the temperature and enhance the neutral-probe horizon emission factor relative to classical BTZ.

title: Reconciling Models for Infinite-Layer Nickelate Superconductors: Role of Interstitial-$s$ Band or $A$-Pocket
comment: 18 pages in total, 13 figures and 4 tables, in the main text and supplementary material. Accepted for publication in Chinese Physics Letters
summary: Understanding the minimal model that captures the essential physics of infinite-layer nickelate superconductors remains a central challenge. Using first-principles density-functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT), we compute and compare the strongly correlated electronic structures and optical spectra of various effective models for the infinite-layer nickelate LaNiO$_2$, ranging from a $d_{x^2-y^2}$ 1-band model to a full 6-band model with all Ni-$3d$ plus an interstitial-$s$ orbital. The results demonstrate that Ni-$3d$ 5-band models overestimate the Hundness picture, whereas 6-band models, which explicitly include the interstitial-$s$ band and have an $A$-pocket, recover the characteristic Mottness physics. Importantly, the influence of the interstitial-$s$ band on the correlations of the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ band is negligible. Thus, superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelates can be reliably described within a single-band Hubbard framework, while the accurate description of inter-orbital properties such as (optical) conductivities requires the inclusion of at least the interstitial-$s$ band.

title: Norm Approximation with Linear Growth of Error for Bosonic Dynamics in the Mean-Field Regime
summary: We consider the quantum many-body dynamics of a homogeneous confined Bose gas in three dimensions in the mean-field scaling regime. We study the Cauchy problem for a class of initial data describing finitely many excitations over a Bose-Einstein condensate. Using a rigorous version of Bogolyubov's theory, we prove that the many-body evolution can be approximated in Fock space norm by a quasifree evolution of the excitations with an error which grows linearly in time. In distinction from earlier results, the slow growth in time holds even though the effective equation is not dispersive.

title: Synthesis-route-dependent state selection in the frustrated spinel ZnV$_2$O$_4$
summary: The emergent properties of strongly correlated materials can be highly sensitive to how they are made, yet synthesis pathway is rarely treated as a fundamental variable governing their ground states. The spinel ZnV$_2$O$_4$ provides a model system in which to test this idea: its pyrochlore lattice of antiferromagnetically coupled V$^{3+}$ $S=1$ moments hosts competing spin and orbital degeneracies, while different synthesis routes yield markedly different low-temperature behaviour. Here, we show that changing the solid-state synthesis pathway reproducibly selects a distinct structural and magnetic ground state. Microwave-assisted solid-state synthesis (MASS) stabilises the cubic spinel structure to low temperature, suppressing the conventional cubic-to-tetragonal transition and preserving the highly frustrated $S=1$ pyrochlore lattice. Combining high-resolution diffraction, magnetometry and inelastic neutron scattering, we find a magnetic ground state exhibiting persistent spin-liquid-like dynamics together with partial spin freezing. Our results establish synthesis pathway as an experimental variable for selecting between competing emergent states in strongly correlated materials, revealing a route to accessing ground states not realised by conventional synthesis.

title: Interface Weyl electrons in the kagome-bilayers
summary: What makes a topological character prominent is whether its characteristic electronic states are located near the Fermi energy. While the kagome-metals possess unique topological characteristics owing to their distinctive electronic band structures, i.e. flat and Dirac bands, the control of Fermi energy to accentuate these characteristics has scarcely been studied in these materials. Here, we propose a new concept for activating the topological characteristics of Weyl electrons specifically near the interface of kagome-bilayers, namely interface Weyl electrons. The kagome-bilayers prepared by a sputtering technique surprisingly exhibit atomically abrupt interfaces thanks to the suppression of interdiffusion for maintaining the crystal symmetry of the hexagonal-type D0$_{19}$ and cubic-type L1$_{2}$ structures. Much higher electrical conductivity of the kagome-bilayers compared to single-layer films indicates the emergent contribution of a highly conductive electronic state at the interfaces. The enhanced electrical conductivity and the exceptionally large anomalous Hall conductivity about 2000 $Ω$$^{-1}$cm$^{-1}$ in the intrinsic mechanism indicates that the emergent interface electronic states comprise Weyl nodes in the D0$_{19}$ structure identified in our theoretical band calculations, triggered by nontrivial charge transfer. These results demonstrate that topological transport can be engineered at the interface of intermetallic compounds, leading further design principles towards development of device functionality.

title: Persistent Hydration and Ionic Mobility: When the Ion Is Not the Only Transported Species
summary: Small-ion transport in water remains only partially understood despite more than a century of theoretical work. The difficulty is especially acute for strongly hydrated ions such as Li$^{+}$, Mg$^{2+}$, and Ca$^{2+}$, whose first hydration shells can persist on timescales comparable to or longer than translational motion. We develop a molecular framework in which the ion, its first hydration shell, and the outer solvent are treated as dynamically coupled components. Local hydration structure and exchange are represented through a potential of mean force and coordination dynamics, while collective solvent response is described through molecular memory functions. The theory clarifies why hydration cannot generally be represented by an additive friction or a single enlarged radius, and provides a route beyond conventional continuum and molecular descriptions.

title: Wegner model in high dimension: singular continuous spectrum from U(1) symmetry breaking and AAT self-consistency
summary: We analyze the energy-spectral decomposition of the Wegner one-orbital model in high lattice dimension using ideas from field theory and statistical mechanics. Most notably, we identify a local spectral measure of singular continuous type for the disordered model at the Anderson transition. The key mechanism that leads to a singular continuous spectrum is a novel scenario of spontaneous symmetry breaking, intimately connected to the non-compactness of the global symmetry group of the field theory. While that symmetry breaks down to a compact subgroup in the metallic phase, it spontaneously breaks down to a nilpotent subgroup at criticality. We describe the symmetry-breaking extremal states approximately, by applying the self-consistent theory of localization due to Abou-Chacra, Anderson, and Thouless. The thrust of our work is to provide a field-theoretical foundation for disorder phenomena associated with singular continuous spectra.

title: Towards Cryogenic AI Hardware: Over 99% Precision In-Memory Computing at 4 K with 3-bit Ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 Capacitors
summary: High-accuracy cryogenic hyperdimensional computing (HDC) is demonstrated using Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) ferroelectric capacitors (FeCAPs) as multilevel analog memories for capacitive compute in-memory (CIM) architectures. On the ISOLET spoken-word dataset, FeCAP-stored vectors achieve up to 92% classification accuracy at 4 K, while charge-domain matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) exhibits near-ideal behaviour with linearity of 1 and error probability below 1% for 4x4 and 4x8 configurations, operating below 3 V. Unlike the performance at 300 K, HDC and CIM at 4 K remains resilient to electric-field-cycling-induced fatigue, thanks to enhanced cryogenic device characteristics, including reduced state variability, strongly suppressed leakage current and stable retention, as well as 78% faster switching. Furthermore, these multibit FeCAPs exhibit endurance beyond 1E9 cycles with polarization degradation below 8%, preserving multilevel integrity. Benefits can also be observed at 300 K, following cooldown and wake-up pulsing at 4 K and subsequent warming up. These results establish multibit FeCAPs as a highly reliable, ultra-low-energy, and accurate analog CIM platform for future cryogenic AI-computing hardware.

title: The Holomorphic-Topological Poisson Sigma Model and Quantization of Affine W-algebras
summary: We construct explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine $W$-algebras for every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model of A. Khan and K. Zeng. A linear differential-graded presentation identifies the universal bulk with Chern--Simons theory near a principal nilpotent background, where holomorphic gauge gives a finite, 1-loop exact quantization. The quantum oper boundary observables form the principal affine $W$-algebra at level $k-h^\vee\hbar$; we also obtain this level shift directly for affine current algebras. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we prove a perturbative quantum equivalence between Chern--Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity, including their oper and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and determine the quantum relation between their parameters.

title: Charged Schrödinger blocks in $1+1$ dimensions from the quartic Casimir and endpoint equations
summary: We construct charge-two Schrödinger conformal blocks in one spatial dimension, independently of any dynamical realization. We consider ordered vacuum four-point functions of fundamental fields of dimension $1/2$, with homogeneous Schrödinger equations at the earliest and latest insertions and interactions allowed in the intermediate two-particle interval. For reduced blocks analytic in signed spatial coordinates and even under simultaneous spatial inversion, two functions of the time cross-ratio determine the full spatial dependence: the collinear value and a rescaled mixed spatial derivative. An exact Kummer lift, built from confluent hypergeometric functions, gives this reconstruction. An operator identity reduces the quartic Casimir equation, modulo the endpoint equations, to an equivalent coupled system for this pair. At generic exchanged dimension, OPE conditions select a unique block up to normalization for each primary parity. We obtain collinear ${}_4F_3$ functions and sums of Kummer products, including the shadow branches. The blocks depend on the relative sign of the signed coordinates, distinguishing piecewise linear worldlines with an inflection from those with monotone segment velocities. In the Calogero model, we recover the previously derived bosonic four-point function and obtain its fermionic counterpart, with an independent integral check. At the diffusion-limited fixed point of $A+B\to\emptyset$, two blocks of opposite primary parity give the same collinear unlike-species response. Nonnegativity for all positions and ordered times selects the even family, thereby establishing that the response summed over species contains the even shadow pair with dimensions $Δ=1,2$. The nonnegativity argument demonstrates a concrete constraint for a Schrödinger bootstrap beyond collinear data.

title: Implementation of LDA+Gutzwiller with Newton's method
comment: 14 pages, 8 figures. Authors' version of the article published in Chin. Phys. B 26, 017103 (2017)
summary: In order to calculate the electronic structure of correlated materials, we propose implementation of the LDA+Gutzwiller method with Newton's method. The self-consistence process, efficiency and convergence of calculation are improved dramatically by using Newton's method with golden section search and other improvement approaches. We compare the calculated results by applying the previous linear mix method and Newton's method. We have applied our code to study the electronic structure of several typical strong correlated materials, including SrVO$_3$, LaCoO$_3$, and La$_2$O$_3$Fe$_2$Se$_2$. Our results fit quite well with the previous studies.

title: Electrostatic and Quantum Transport Engineering of Multilayer Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions for Improved TER and RA Trade off
summary: Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for non-volatile memory and neuromorphic computing, but achieving a high tunnel electroresistance ratio (TER) with a low resistance-area (RA) product remains challenging. In this work, TiN/Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$ (HZO)-based FTJs containing zero to three TiO$_2$ and IGZO-based quantum wells (QWs) are analyzed using the Miller ferroelectric (FE) polarization model integrated with the non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism to examine the effects of QW material and thickness on polarization and transport. TiO$_2$-based structures exhibit higher polarization and TER than IGZO-based structures. At a read bias of 0.1 V, the uniform TiO$_2$ double-QW structure, with 1-nm-thick QW and insulating layer (IL) layers, gives a TER of $2.71\times10^{10}\%$ and an RA product of $5\times10^4~Ω\cdot\text{cm}^2$, compared with $5.95\times10^7\%$ and $2\times10^5~Ω\cdot\text{cm}^2$, respectively, for IGZO. Both uniform and non-uniform TiO$_2$ double-QW structures exhibit resonant tunneling (RT) and negative differential resistance (NDR) associated with QW-confined states. Increasing the first QW thickness to 1.38 nm, while keeping the second QW and both IL layers at 1 nm, shifts the confined-state energies and modifies resonant transport. The selected non-uniform structure achieves a TER of $2.95\times10^{11}\%$ and an RA product of $1.25\times10^3~Ω\cdot\text{cm}^2$ at a read bias of 0.1 V. Elastic scattering changes the amplitude and width of QW resonant-transmission peaks, with a stronger effect on the low resistance state (LRS) than on the high resistance state (HRS). These results show that QW material and thickness optimization can improve the TER--RA trade-off, while electrode screening and elastic scattering further influence polarization-dependent transport in multilayer FTJs.

title: Finite-time stochastic resetting in bounded domains: competing targets, energetic cost, and optimal search strategies
summary: We investigate the first-passage dynamics and energetic cost of a Brownian particle subject to finite-time stochastic resetting in a bounded one-dimensional domain with two absorbing boundaries. Unlike conventional instantaneous resetting, the particle is returned to a prescribed resetting position through a finite-duration process driven by a linear trapping potential. By solving the corresponding backward equations, we derive analytical expressions for the mean global first-passage time and the splitting probabilities. Our results show that the finite duration of the return process can substantially modify the dependence of the mean global first-passage time on the resetting rate. In particular, we identify a critical trapping strength above which resetting can accelerate the search process, and characterize how the range of favorable resetting positions depends on the trapping strength. We further characterize the energetic cost of resetting by deriving the generating function of the total work and obtaining an analytical expression for its mean value. For the linear trapping potential considered here, we establish an exact relation between the mean total work and the mean cumulative return time. This relation allows us to establish a quantitative trade-off between the mean global first-passage time and the energetic expenditure, revealing how the finite duration of the return process affects search efficiency. Brownian dynamics simulations confirm our theoretical predictions.

title: Free energy distribution for two non-crossing directed polymers on the cylinder
summary: We consider the partition sum $Z_L(t)$ of two non-crossing continuum directed polymers of length $t$, in a common random medium with the geometry of a cylinder of circumference length $L$. In the limit $t \to +\infty$, the $k$-th cumulant of (minus) the free energy $\log Z_L(t)$, grows as $c_k(L) t$, and we compute the amplitudes $c_k(L)$. To this aim we first study the integer moments $\langle Z_L(t)^n \rangle$, whose long-time behavior is determined by the ground-state energy of the one-dimensional attractive Lieb--Liniger model in the symmetry sector associated with the Young diagram $(n,n)$ (a two-component bosonic nested Bethe ansatz). This ground state energy is obtained using the nested Bethe-Ansatz involving $2n$ physical rapidities and $n$ auxiliary rapidities. The analytic continuation in the replica number $n$, which yields the cumulants $c_k(L)$, is performed through a non-trivial generalization of the method developed by Brunet and Derrida for a single polymer on the cylinder. We obtain fully explicit formulas for the mean $c_1(L)$ and the variance $c_2(L)$, and construct a systematic scheme for computing all higher cumulants $c_k(L)$. Finally, taking $L\to+\infty$ and $n\to0$ with $nL^{1/2}$ fixed, we derive a universal scaling function which characterizes the large-deviation statistics of the two-polymer free energy and is expected to be universal within the one-dimensional two-layer periodic SHE/KPZ class. The two tails of the large-deviation function are obtained analytically, revealing different roles of the non-crossing constraint in favorable and unfavorable fluctuations of the common disorder.

title: Predicting solid-state reaction onset temperatures from high-throughput pairwise synthesis
comment: 78 pages, 6 main manuscript figures, supplemental information included
summary: Solid-state synthesis still relies on heuristics to choose reaction temperatures. The most widely used, Tammann's rule, places reaction onset at two-thirds of the lowest precursor melting point, but has never been systematically tested. Using an automated laboratory, we heated 1,035 pairwise combinations of 46 common precursors at their Tammann temperatures and identified the products by x-ray diffraction. Only 25% of pairs formed products containing both precursors. Combining these outcomes with text-mined literature syntheses, we trained log-normal accelerated failure time models that treat each fixed-temperature experiment as a bound on the unknown onset temperature. On 26 reactions with onset temperatures measured by in situ x-ray diffraction, a three-descriptor model reduced the mean absolute error from 131°C (Tammann's rule) to 88°C; adding 29 further physicochemical descriptors did not improve the model. Reaction onset can therefore be predicted from routine pass/fail synthesis outcomes, and predictions will improve as such data accumulates.

title: Melvin-type Electromagnetized Kerr Black Hole in Kaluza-Klein and Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion Theories
summary: A naive application of solution-generating techniques to construct Melvin-type rotating black holes in the Kaluza-Klein (KK) theory in the presence of both electric and magnetic external fields generically introduces an undesirable Taub-swirling twist term. We investigate its origin and modify the electromagnetization procedure, thereby constructing an exact solution of the Melvin-type electromagnetized Kerr black hole in the KK theory without the swirling term. We also obtain the analogous solution in the Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion (EMDA) theory. The modified solution-generating techniques allow one to introduce both the dyonic charges and external electromagnetic fields independently into Ricci-flat seed metrics in both theories, without generating either Taub-NUT or Taub-swirling twists.

title: Spectrum of the parity operator for parafermions and parabosons from character formulas
summary: In a recent paper [J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 59 175201 (2026)] Green's triple relations for parafermions and parabosons were extended by including a new operator $P$, referred to as the parity operator. The spectrum of $P$ in Fock space representations was computed, making use of the action of parafermion (resp.\ paraboson) creation and annihilation operators. In the current paper, we adopt a different method to compute the spectrum of $P$, namely using character formulas. For a set of $n$ parafermions, the action of $P$ is deduced from character formulas of $so(2n+2)$. For a set of $n$ parabosons, the known spectrum of $P$ yields new character formulas of particular $osp(2|2n)$ representations.

title: Local spin constraints and symmetry in single-$Q$ spiral magnets
summary: The Luttinger--Tisza (LT) method provides a lower bound on the energy of classical spin models but relaxes the local spin-length constraints. For a generic incommensurate single-$Q$ spiral, fixed spin length requires circular polarization on every magnetic sublattice, a condition not guaranteed by equal sublattice weights in the lowest LT eigenmode. We develop a constrained formulation for general bilinear classical spin Hamiltonians with one or two magnetic sublattices. For one sublattice, minimization reduces to a secular equation for the spiral-plane normal. For two sublattices, exact elimination of the relative phase gives a frame-independent energy on the space of two unit normals. We derive symmetry constraints by distinguishing operations that preserve or reverse the Fourier arm and those that preserve or exchange sublattices. For a model with symmetric anisotropy, numerical optimization over both spiral-plane normals yields a lower energy than either constrained pure exchange-sector state, despite the block diagonalization of the linear Hamiltonian. A separate anisotropic two-sublattice benchmark demonstrates that enforcing local circularity can shift the preferred ordering wave vector even when the lowest LT eigenmode has equal sublattice weights.

authors: R. L. Silva. R. C. Silva
title: Conformal defects in a quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev chain: an exactly parametrized Ising defect line and a relevant vacancy
summary: The quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev chain of coupled hexagonal plaquettes recently introduced by Majumder is exactly solvable in terms of free Majorana fermions and undergoes a topological transition at the exchange anisotropy $J_x=\sqrt{2}\,J$. By eliminating the two-coordinated sites of each plaquette we reduce the zero-energy problem to a uniform Majorana chain, which yields the critical point, a single Majorana cone at $k=0$ (hence an Ising critical point with central charge $c=\tfrac12$), and closed forms for every defect quantity that follows. A weakened inter-plaquette bond $λJ_x$ is an exactly marginal defect with transmission $T=4λ^2/(1+λ^2)^2$ at low energy, that is, $T=\sin^2 2φ$ with $\tanφ=λ$: the bond traverses the ferromagnetic defect line of the Ising conformal field theory from the transparent point to the cut chain, and we give its exact energy dependence on the lattice. The intra-plaquette bonds land on the same line with different parametrizations: a $y$ or $z$ bond has $\tanφ=(1+λ)/2$ and covers only $T\in[0.64,1]$, because the plaquette provides a parallel path, whereas an $x$ bond has $\tanφ=(1+λ)/2λ$ and covers the strong-link half of the line, $φ\in(π/4,π/2)$. The identification is closed by an independent observable: the coefficient of $\ln L$ in the entanglement entropy across the defect follows the conformal-field-theory function $σ(\sqrt T)/2$ of Brehm and Brunner to within $0.4\%$ along the whole line, with no adjustable parameter. A vacancy behaves in the opposite way. It never binds a plaquette flux, because plaquettes share no sites, but it leaves its singly bonded neighbor as a conserved classical spin whose dangling Majorana is a zero-energy resonance.

title: Blanket theory for dense networks
summary: We show how Blanket theory provides a constructive method for calculating cavity functionals in dense spin networks. Building on the description through interfaces and magnetization shells, we develop the calculation from the low-temperature fluctuations around the ground state. In this regime, dilute defects reveal the mechanism of random energy model (REM) universality for linear energies, while their sharing and renewal across layers organize the energies and Gibbs weights into a hierarchy. Because the same configurations determine the covariances of the fresh cavity fields, this construction identifies the fields and weights with an Aizenman-Sims-Starr random overlap structure. The cavity contributions can then be evaluated through recursive fractional means, yielding an explicit free-energy functional parametrized by layer magnetizations and hierarchical exponents, with coefficients determined by the interaction variances and the network normalization. Under the stated moment and normalization conditions, comparison of pressures transfers the limiting mean pressure from the Gaussian representative to networks with independent centered non-Gaussian couplings having the same variances. We illustrate the method with the deterministic Curie-Weiss model, recover the Parisi functional for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, and derive the functionals for restricted and deep Boltzmann machines, including the full replica symmetry breaking (fullRSB) limit.

title: A Monte Carlo study of closely packed two-patch particles with frustrated interactions
summary: Recently it was found that closely packed two-patch particles exhibit rich orientational ordering behaviors, e.g., nonmonotonic changes of the nematic order parameter and double BKT phase transitions [arXiv:2509.03981]. In this work, we show that, with repulsive patch-patch, attractive patch-nonpatch and intermediate nonpatch-nonpatch interactions, there exist frustrations in the system of closely packed two-patch particles. To investigate the ground states of the system, we design a Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm with single-defect propagation. The simulation results show that the ground states are disordered and the correlation functions decay exponentially with the distance. These results demonstrate that in 2D close packing one could design patchy particles to explore orientationally disordered systems.

title: Application of Pretrained Universal Machine Learning Force-Fields for Phase Transitions Prediction in ZrO2
comment: 23 pages, 13 figures, 1 supplementary table, 7 supplementary figures. Supplementary Material included
summary: Pretrained universal machine-learning force fields can reduce the cost of finite-temperature molecular dynamics relative to density functional theory. However, most benchmarks test only static properties and do not assess whether these models reproduce the correct phase-transition sequence. Here, we benchmark ten open-source universal machine-learning force fields for zirconia (ZrO$_2$) using phonon dispersion calculations and variable-cell isothermal-isobaric molecular dynamics. Zirconia is a useful test because it has three thermodynamically stable crystalline phases prior to melting, following the sequence monoclinic-tetragonal-cubic. Four models reproduce this sequence: 7net-l3i5, MatterSim-v1.0.0-1M, MACE-mpa, and MACE-D3. Models with orthorhombic-tetragonal energy errors above about 10 meV/atom (7net-0, CHGNet, and MACE) instead produce an orthorhombic intermediate and predict monoclinic-orthorhombic-tetragonal-cubic-liquid upon heating. ORB-based models fail to sustain stable variable-cell dynamics because their phonon frequencies are compressed by 30-60% relative to the density functional theory reference. Across all ten models, two ground-state diagnostics predict finite-temperature behavior. Relative polymorph energetics should agree with the matched density functional theory reference within about 6 meV/atom, and the phonon spectrum should not show systematic softening. These diagnostics are practical screening metrics for assessing pretrained force fields for phase-transition predictions.

title: Non-Perturbative Moduli Stabilization with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ Modular Symmetry
summary: We study the stabilization of the three complex moduli associated with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ modular symmetry by gaugino condensation in $\mathcal N=1$ supergravity models from heterotic string theory, where one-loop threshold corrections fix both the modular weight and the singularity structure of the superpotential. We determine, for each threshold class, the complete parametrization of the consistent superpotential relying on Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ basic modular-invariant ratios and their syzygies, generalizing the insufficient SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$-inspired techniques based solely on polynomials of its absolute invariants. This structure supports a rich landscape of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua. Unlike in the SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$ case, higher-order zeros produce continuous surfaces and curves of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua, while, among the six isolated fixed points, only those with $S_4$ and $D_{12}$ residual symmetries can stabilize all three moduli. We also construct isolated vacua away from fixed points, some of which lie at the moduli values preferred by genus-two modular flavor fits, and examine the suppression of the geometric moduli masses near an enhanced-symmetry point.

title: Free energy distribution for two non-crossing directed polymers on the cylinder
summary: We consider the partition sum $Z_L(t)$ of two non-crossing continuum directed polymers of length $t$, in a common random medium with the geometry of a cylinder of circumference length $L$. In the limit $t \to +\infty$, the $k$-th cumulant of (minus) the free energy $\log Z_L(t)$, grows as $c_k(L) t$, and we compute the amplitudes $c_k(L)$. To this aim we first study the integer moments $\langle Z_L(t)^n \rangle$, whose long-time behavior is determined by the ground-state energy of the one-dimensional attractive Lieb--Liniger model in the symmetry sector associated with the Young diagram $(n,n)$ (a two-component bosonic nested Bethe ansatz). This ground state energy is obtained using the nested Bethe-Ansatz involving $2n$ physical rapidities and $n$ auxiliary rapidities. The analytic continuation in the replica number $n$, which yields the cumulants $c_k(L)$, is performed through a non-trivial generalization of the method developed by Brunet and Derrida for a single polymer on the cylinder. We obtain fully explicit formulas for the mean $c_1(L)$ and the variance $c_2(L)$, and construct a systematic scheme for computing all higher cumulants $c_k(L)$. Finally, taking $L\to+\infty$ and $n\to0$ with $nL^{1/2}$ fixed, we derive a universal scaling function which characterizes the large-deviation statistics of the two-polymer free energy and is expected to be universal within the one-dimensional two-layer periodic SHE/KPZ class. The two tails of the large-deviation function are obtained analytically, revealing different roles of the non-crossing constraint in favorable and unfavorable fluctuations of the common disorder.

title: Molecular Kondo Ball Based on an Endohedral Fullerene
summary: We theoretically predict a molecular Kondo ball in TiSc$_2$N@C$_{80}$/Al(111), where a Ti-centered $S = 1/2$ local moment is encapsulated within a closed fullerene $π$ cage that serves as an itinerant-like electronic reservoir for Kondo screening. First-principles calculations show that intermediate molecule--substrate hybridization broadens the discrete C$_{80}$ molecular levels into itinerant-like electronic states while preserving the Ti local moment, with similar electronic conditions found for Cd(0001) and In(101).Hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) simulations reveal a temperature-dependent Fano resonance with a Kondo temperature of about 60 K.The key electronic characteristics underlying the Kondo state remain robust against adsorption orientation, demonstrating that the closed cage geometry provides an orientation-tolerant molecular architecture for Kondo screening.

title: Geometric Decomposition of Entropy Production Based on General $f$-Divergences
summary: We construct a general class of excess--housekeeping decompositions of entropy production based on $f$-divergences for overdamped Langevin systems. The excess entropy production rate equals the relaxation rate of the $f$-divergence toward a relaxation target and also admits an optimal-transport representation, while the housekeeping velocity preserves the same relaxation target. Our framework recovers the Hatano--Sasa and Maes--Neto{č}n{ý} decompositions as special cases, and unifies their relaxational and optimal-transport aspects within a common structure. Moreover, our framework yields physically meaningful decompositions beyond these two by taking a desired distribution as the relaxation target.

title: Fast closed-loop STEM navigation using vision-language models with typed decisions
summary: Closed-loop scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), in which each acquired image determines the next field of view and magnification, offers a route to autonomous atomic-scale materials analysis. Such a loop would automate navigation to defects and grain boundaries, a task that has long relied on operator judgment, and would enable systematic analysis of diverse local structures at scale. Realizing it hinges on the decision step, which must translate each acquired image into the next operation both quickly and correctly; yet which decision method can deliver both remains unclear. Here, we isolate this decision step. Using simulated atomic-resolution STEM images of a substitutional W dopant and a grain boundary in monolayer MoS$_2$, where the true target position is known and every method starts from identical conditions, we compared four vision-language models (VLMs) and three decision methods. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of Typed Decision, which directly obtains the probabilities of candidate labels from a pretrained VLM, for closed-loop STEM navigation. Typed Decision showed the shortest decision latency for all models (0.13-0.21 s) and generally achieved the highest navigation success rate among the three methods: it was the best for all models in W dopant navigation (66-91%) and for the best-performing model, Cosmos-Reason2 32B, in grain boundary navigation (43%). Furthermore, navigation to the different targets, the W dopant and the grain boundary, was possible by natural-language specification alone, without task-specific training of the VLM. These results indicate that Typed Decision is an effective decision method for realizing fast, accurate, and flexible closed-loop STEM.

title: Scalar/axion Wormholes and Boundary Conditions in Gravitational Path Integrals
summary: Recent work noted that whether or not a given class of spacetime wormholes contributes to the gravitational path integral can depend strongly on the choice of boundary conditions. In particular, for asymptotically-AdS scalar/axion wormholes with spherical boundaries it was suggested that there are regimes where the same wormhole contributes to a Euclidean low-energy effective field theory computation of the partition function $Z_N$ defined by imposing Neumann boundary conditions on the scalar/axion field, while it fails to contribute to a corresponding partition function $Z_D$ defined by imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions on this field. Here we investigate toy models of related wormholes associated with JT gravity coupled to a scalar field, asymptotically-AdS gravity coupled to an axion/scalar with toroidal boundary conditions, and asymptotically flat gravity coupled to an axion/scalar. In all cases we compare $Z_D$ and $Z_N$ as computed in a truncated low-energy effective theory by an appropriate integral over constrained wormholes. In each case we find that, even though $Z_D$ and $Z_N$ are related by an integral transform, the two generally receive contributions from differing sets of saddles. Along the way, we uncover a variety of additional interesting subtleties associated with semiclassical contributions to our $Z_D$ and $Z_N$.

title: Multiplicity criteria for the absolutely continuous spectrum of finite hopping Hermitian operators
summary: We consider locally finite-hopping Hermitian operators that admit radial-type transfer matrix sets in the sense of Sadel. We extend his spectral averaging formula from scalar spectral measures to matrix-valued spectral measures associated to a root matrix. This extension yields criteria for lower bounds on the multiplicity of absolutely continuous spectrum. As applications, we consider random decaying shell-matrix potentials on stair-like graphs with increasing-width wires and operators on the Bethe lattice. In both cases, we establish that absolutely continuous spectrum has almost surely infinite multiplicity.

title: Stabilizer models of achiral abelian topological orders
summary: We construct continuous-variable stabilizer codes realizing every achiral 2D abelian topological order, both bosonic and fermionic. Starting from an arbitrary signature-zero integer $K$-matrix, we show that the corresponding topological order can be obtained by condensing a lattice of dyons with trivial pairwise mutual braiding in an $\mathbb{R}^N$ gauge theory. We implement this condensation microscopically by gauging a non-on-site 1-form symmetry of the $\mathbb{R}^N$ toric code.

title: Neither graphs nor hypergraphs: structural moments of higher-order interactions determine stochastic social-impact dynamics
summary: Whether higher-order interactions can be reduced to simpler representations is a question about the dynamics they drive, not only about their structure: what can be discarded is whatever the dynamics does not see. We make this precise for binary-state stochastic dynamics in which each agent, when updated, interacts with a randomly selected group and changes state according to the fraction of disagreeing members, as in generalized voter and social-impact models on hypergraphs. We ask which statistics of the group-interaction process determine the resulting Markov dynamics. For response functions that are polynomials of degree $q$, the answer is a hierarchy of size-weighted inclusion moments, which we call structural moments, involving at most $q$ neighbors at a time, regardless of how large the groups are. These moments are not only sufficient but also necessary: two interaction structures produce identical dynamics for all such rules if and only if their moments coincide. More generally, each class of rules selects its own minimal structural description, ranging from weighted pairwise links for linear rules to the full distribution of co-membership by group size for arbitrary rules. For voter-type rules, the same moments also reconstruct exact pairwise copying representations of these dynamics.

title: Physics-Guided Crystal Structure Elucidation from Powder X-Ray Diffraction with Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
comment: 15 pages, 7 figures. Supporting Information is available as an ancillary file
summary: Determining unique atomic coordinates from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) remains challenging because peak overlap, weak scattering from light elements, limited scattering contrast between elements with similar atomic numbers, and experimental noise render the inverse problem underdetermined. Here, we present XCAPE (XRD-Constrained Accelerated Prediction Engine), a crystal structure prediction (CSP) framework that integrates experimentally derived composition, unit cell parameters, space group, and PXRD data into a symmetry-aware evolutionary search. XCAPE explores Wyckoff-site configurations using tailored mutation operations, evaluates candidates by both energetic stability and diffraction agreement, and accelerates geometry optimization using a universal machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP). The framework recovered 71 of 77 database-derived benchmark structures (92.2%) from simulated PXRD patterns and all 12 reference structures from experimental PXRD patterns. It further identified 12 candidate structure assignments that are consistent with experimental PXRD patterns, lack matching entries in the Inorganic Crystal Structure Database (ICSD), and are thermodynamically competitive at the MLIP level. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations showed that 10 of these 12 candidates lie within 10 meV/atom of the convex hull. By bridging experimental diffraction data and physically plausible atomistic models, XCAPE can provide structural insight into previously unresolved materials and support accelerated materials discovery in automated research workflows.

title: ER=EPR and IMP wormholes in quantum gravity
summary: We analyze and refine the ER=EPR conjecture by studying IMP (Isenberg, Mazzeo and Pollack \cite{Isenberg:2001qe}) wormholes in QFT and quantum gravity, in the AdS/CFT context. IMP wormholes are solutions to the Einstein equations constructed from another general solution of Einstein's equations by gluing a handle on a Cauchy slice with a constant mean curvature, so that the initial data on the slice does not change in the regions away from the handle. This is made possible by using what is called the conformal method. This same method also enables one to recover a well defined perturbation theory in quantum gravity, and particularly for asymptotically AdS spacetimes \cite{Witten:2022xxp}. Thus we construct the perturbation theory on these backgrounds in addition to exploring ER=EPR when $G_{N}=0$, in the limit it is perturbatively small and beyond perturbation theory.

title: On the thermal behavior of composites embedding extended general interfaces
summary: In heterogeneous materials, surface roughness, chemical incompatibility, mechanical mismatch or manufacturing defects result in imperfect bonding between the constituents. Such imperfections introduce a finite-thickness interphase zone between the constituents that possess a graded or inhomogeneous micro-structure. It is virtually impossible to resolve the behavior of such interphases. Instead, a well-established approach is to replace the interphase by a zero-thickness interface endowed with its own energetic structure. Conventional interface models define the interface temperature as an average of the temperatures of the surrounding bulk phases. However, this assumption is only adequate to represent uniform homogeneous interphases and it fails to accurately capture the behavior of graded or inhomogeneous interphases. In this work, we address this limitation by allowing for unequal contributions of the surrounding bulk phases to the interface temperature. We systematically revisit the resulting balance equations and present the computational framework for the finite element implementation of the model. We further incorporate the proposed model within the homogenization framework and derive closed-form analytical expressions for the effective thermal conductivity of fiber- and particle-reinforced composites, accouting for the influence of the extended general interface. Finally, through a series of numerical examples, we demonstrate the capabilities of the proposed model and investigate the influence of its parameters on the size-dependent thermal behavior of composites.

title: Hidden topological signatures in a van der Waals ferromagnet revealed by spin-resolved circular-dichroic photoemission
summary: Layered ferromagnets with strongly correlated electrons provide a platform for exploring the interplay among magnetism, spin-orbit coupling, and nontrivial band topology. $\mathrm{Ni}_{1/4}\mathrm{TaSe}_2$ is a correlated van der Waals ferromagnet with a transition temperature of 58 K that lies close in composition to a superconducting phase that emerges upon Ni depletion. Here, we combine spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, circular-dichroism measurements, and density functional theory calculations to investigate its spin-resolved electronic structure. We observe spin-polarized states crossing the Fermi level and signatures of broken time-reversal symmetry in the ferromagnetic state. Spin-resolved circular-dichroism measurements further reveal a helicity-dependent spin response consistent with a finite spin Berry curvature and suggestive of local topological character. Together, these results establish an experimental connection between ferromagnetism, spin-polarized electronic states, and topological signatures in $\mathrm{Ni}_{1/4}\mathrm{TaSe}_2$, providing a foundation for investigating how these properties may relate to the emergence of superconductivity upon Ni depletion.

title: Phase transitions in work fluctuations in correlated N-particle resets
summary: Systems of $N$ independent uncorrelated particles subjected to the same stochastic change in the environment have recently been studied both theoretically and in experiments, to elucidate the interesting phenomenon of dynamically emergent interparticle positional correlations. However, the thermodynamic cost of creating such correlations, as well as its interplay with the initial distribution of the $N$ particles has not been studied. In this paper, we study systems of $N$ particles that are simultaneously subjected to a switch of an external potential, either stochastically or periodically, beginning from arbitrarily correlated initial states. We map out the distribution of thermodynamic work for such a system in the full parameter space of the problem that includes the number of particles $N$, arbitrary initial correlations between particles and arbitrary initial reduced single particle distributions. We demonstrate that the parameter space is partitioned non-trivially, and in an $N$-dependent way, into distinct "phases", whereby the functional form of the variance of the work changes discontinuously across phases. The number of such phases depends on the source of stochasticity in the dynamics.

title: Materials representations organize transferable supervision for chemical extrapolation
summary: Materials discovery often requires chemical extrapolation beyond labeled data. When target compounds contain elements absent from training, which compounds of other elements provide transferable supervision remains unclear. Here we show that, without target-property labels, materials representations rank other elements by the supervision their compounds provide. Engineered descriptors rank them largely by elemental-property similarity, whereas a pretrained crystal-graph encoder ranks them by the geometry of its learned representation. At fixed training-set size, excluding the compounds of the encoder's six top-ranked elements raises formation-energy and bandgap errors by 100-110 meV per atom and 42-85 meV, versus little change for six lower-ranked elements. The rankings hold across properties, regressors and datasets. The encoder's ranking outperforms elemental-property similarity and periodic groups, suggesting that it captures how elements behave within compounds. Materials representations thus organize transferable supervision, which can be identified before model training, informing dataset assessment and label acquisition.

title: Folded out-of-time-order correlators in double-scaled SYK
summary: Harlow and Zhao arXiv:2607.14215 have identified ``anti-scrambling'' as a characteristic signature of cosmological horizons in de Sitter space, and proposed that it can be realized in a quantum system with bounded energy by Euclidean time ``folding" of out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs). We implement this prescription in the DSSYK model. We use arXiv:2303.03474 to define an infinite-temperature ($β=0$) DSSYK OTOC that in the semiclassical limit of small values of the double-scaling parameter $λ$ reproduces the usual AdS eikonal shockwave behavior with its characteristic time delay, and then apply the Harlow-Zhao fold with the ``fake'' DSSYK inverse temperature $β_f$ playing the role of $β$. We demonstrate both numerically and analytically that the resulting folded OTOC displays anti-scrambling. The exact DSSYK evaluation tracks the semiclassical de Sitter eikonal formula in the scrambling regime, including a time advance instead of a time delay.The direction of the fold selects the side from which the continued eikonal amplitude approaches its branch cut. We show how our results are consistent with recent ``no-go" constraints. We compare the folded correlator with the two-shell analysis of arXiv:2607.14215: the growing term of the two-shell dilaton invariant appears in DSSYK with the same exponent, but as an imaginary part, while its real part, which would signal the backreaction that ends in a crunch, only moves by $O(λ)$ for thermal-scale probes. We also generalize to finite $β$; we find reasonable agreement with the de Sitter eikonal form for sufficiently high temperatures, but at lower temperatures the folded correlator is dominated by a pair of complex conjugate saddles, an anti-Stokes crossover that prevents retrieval of the eikonal behavior from the folded OTOC.

title: Commuting integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs revisited: certified densities, spectral rigidity, and an exact identification at the c=1 branch point
comment: 28 pages. Single consolidated article, per the moderators' invitation (MOD-101633), merging submissions submit/7974478 and submit/7974538
summary: We revisit the commuting local integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs constructed in hep-th/0404195 as input data for integrable boundary states, using exact-arithmetic operator-product engines. A bootstrap lemma reduces its overdetermined bilinear commutativity systems to a distinguished odd charge D plus linear kernel problems -- conditionally on even-spin vacancy, a machine-verified but finite-range input. For the Z_2 x Z_2 "paperclip" family we publish the spin-7 density P_8, prove [I_3,I_5]=[I_3,I_7]=[I_5,I_7]=0 identically in n, and verify the Lukyanov-Vitchev-Zamolodchikov four-screening characterization at spins 7 and 9 at sampled n. For the A_2^(2) family we give an exact Coulomb-gas dictionary to the dual Phi_{1,2}/Phi_{2,1} perturbations (that identification itself being classical, Zamolodchikov; Smirnov), whence the infinite hierarchy at all spins 6n+-1 follows by the Feigin-Frenkel affine-Toda theorem; our contribution is the certified dictionary, not a new all-spin construction. At c=1 the tower's defining charges are exactly quantum KdV at c_{1,4}=-25/2 -- the all-odd sector of the Freeman-Hornfeck-West family: the hierarchy embeds at every odd spin, equality verified through spin 15, all-spin multiplicity one open. We exclude or disfavor the named non-KdV candidates at the tested loci and identify the self-dual degeneracy as L(1,0). Through spin 11, the generic centralizer of I_3 is, for all three Z_2 x O(N) "cylindrical" families, one-dimensional at odd and zero at even spins, with Q(t)-symbolic charges at spins 7, 9, 11 and an explained fiber jump at N=-2. We certify the published 2004 low-spin formulas and record five corrections (one presumed). All-spin statements are made only where proved, finite-range otherwise. We close with a corank-character conjecture linking the rank deficiencies of the bilinear systems to characters of screening kernels.

title: From geometric curvature to effective backgrounds: a dictionary for Dirac fermions in one, two and three spatial dimensions
comment: 19 pages, 5 captioned figures, provisionally accepted in Physica Scripta
summary: Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-algebra identity and follow it through one, two, and three spatial dimensions. Once the spin connection is written in terms of Ricci rotation coefficients, only two contractions can occur. The trace produces a term with the index structure of a vector potential in every dimensionality; it enters with an imaginary factor i and is precisely the term that keeps the operator Hermitian when the Fermi velocity depends on position. The totally antisymmetric contraction produces an object that depends on the number of indices available to the Levi-Civita symbol: a trace on a line, a pseudoscalar mass on a surface, and an axial vector potential in a volume. Neither contraction is invariant under local rotations of the frame, and we give the transformation laws. On a surface, the curl of the trace term can always be removed by a frame rotation, while its divergence is proportional to the Gaussian curvature. We apply the correspondence to a Gaussian bump, where the local density of states at the center falls below its flat value and obeys a closed form at low energy; to a wire, where a nonuniform lapse binds states inside the gap and a nonuniform velocity cannot; to stationary frames on a surface, where a circulating drag shifts the Dirac mass locally with either sign; and to twisted and rotating frames in a volume, where the axial term takes the form of a chiral chemical potential produced by the frame alone, or separates Weyl nodes in a rotating sample. We separate the geometric contribution from the lattice pseudogauge field that dominates the response of strained samples

title: Numerical integration of non-local master equations for renewal shot noise with drift and state-dependent amplitude
summary: The probability density of a system driven by a drift and a renewal train of kicks with state-dependent amplitude obeys a master equation that is non-local in space, because the kick operator $\hat{p}(i\partial_x I(x))$ is of infinite order, and, for non-exponential waiting times, non-local in time, with a memory kernel containing the propagator of the drift. Its solutions contain quasi-singular components, the never-kicked mass, which collapse onto the attractors of the drift. We present an accurate numerical method for such equations. The kick operator is a push-forward along the Marcus flow; in the Lamperti variable it becomes a translation, whose exact cell-to-cell weights follow from the cumulative distribution of the kicks, without quadrature. The drift is integrated by a conservative semi-Lagrangian step exact in time. The memory is represented by a sum of exponentials whose auxiliary fields are advected by the drift, at a cost linear in the number of steps. The never-kicked mass is transported exactly. For each ingredient we quantify the errors of simpler alternatives. The method is verified against exact solutions and event-driven Monte Carlo simulations with exact flow maps, from which it is statistically indistinguishable with $10^8$ trajectories. Parameters tuned for Gaussian kicks carry over unchanged to other kick distributions, and near a zero of the coupling, where the density vanishes faster than any power, the solution follows the known asymptotic law down to densities of order $10^{-37}$, far beyond Monte Carlo reach. As an application we compare the exact equation with its local and Poissonian approximations: in the range explored, the local equation deviates by up to 8% of the density width, also for waiting times with finite mean, consistently with an error estimate predicting larger deviations for slow drifts at long times. A Fortran implementation is available.

title: Tuning spreading transport in GaN HEMTs with an AlN space layer under non-equilibrium heating
summary: Lateral spreading transport dominates near-junction heat dissipation in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, yet thermal control has largely overlooked this geometry. It neither reaches the core AlGaN/GaN region nor, beyond the spatial spreading itself, accounts for the spectral non-equilibrium of the heat source. Here we tune the spreading resistance directly by inserting a thin, highly conducting AlN space layer above the source to intercept heat and divert it laterally. We test this approach across GaN, AlGaN/GaN, and AlGaN/AlN/GaN structures under both equilibrium and longitudinal-optical (LO)-pumped non-equilibrium heating, pairing non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) with full-band phonon Monte Carlo (MC). In equilibrium, the AlN layer lowers the spreading resistance by 38% relative to the AlGaN-capped structure and by 17% relative to bare GaN, with little change in the one-dimensional resistance. The equilibrium color map over AlN thickness and interfacial bonding shows a strong interface effect but a weak thickness trend that reverses, so the gain is set by interface admission rather than solely by thickness or bulk conductivity. This ordering is independently confirmed by gray MC simulations. Under LO pumping, the spreading resistance rises by 58-83% in NEMD and by 9-20% in MC, and the equilibrium spatial optimum weakens or even reverses. This is because an optical-to-acoustic conversion gate now precedes every spatial gate and locks energy in slow optical modes. The three gates in series (optical-to-acoustic conversion, interface admission, and lateral diversion) close into a single non-equilibrium resistance network that predicts the full-band MC cases and frames the AlN space layer as a design variable within the non-equilibrium source state.

title: Holomorphic Feynman diagrams in four dimensions and the quantum BPS ring
summary: We compute, at all loop orders, the kernels of the holomorphic Feynman graphs that carry the loop corrections to supersymmetry transformations and to regularized products of local operators in the holomorphic twist of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric gauge theories. The current equations of these holomorphic graph integrals are those of an electrical network. Schwinger parameters are resistances and holomorphic momenta are injected currents. Iterating series, parallel and star--triangle reductions on Schwinger space gives the fan, spider and cubic product-forest kernels at all loop orders. Assuming that twisting commutes with quantization for these composite operators, we identify the twisted differential with their loop-corrected supersymmetry transformation. We give every perturbative correction to the supersymmetry transformation in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills theory, including its action on operators with arbitrary holomorphic derivatives. Using the marked higher operations of Gaiotto, Kulp and Wu, we also construct and compute the quantum product of operators and prove that, on $\mathbf Q$-cohomology, it is associative, graded commutative and unital, supplying the multiplication of the quantum BPS ring. Every multi-graviton operator thus has an explicit finite completion to a cocycle of the full quantum supercharge. Our computer census finds new fortuitous classes and one-loop lifts in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills theory with several gauge groups. We have found no two-loop lift in the sectors tested. We also find two-loop lifts in the Leigh--Strassler and $β$-deformations of $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills theory. In other theories, we find two-, three- and four-loop lifts in abelian gauge theories, and two- and three-loop lifts in $\mathcal N=2$ $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ gauge theories and their singlet deformations.

title: Exact Solutions to Matrix Models and String Theories: The Global Construction
comment: 190 pages, 68 figures, 3 tables, 4 appendices; 85 plot files, jheppub-nosort.sty
summary: Exact nonperturbative solutions to matrix models and string theories are obtained in closed-form via a discrete-Fourier/Zak-transform representation of their partition-function resurgent-transseries. Examples include all hermitian one-matrix models (paired with their topological string duals) alongside all their multicritical and minimal-string double-scaling limits. The resulting structure is resonant, necessarily including both eigenvalues (D-branes) and anti-eigenvalues (negative-tension-branes). In a complementary preceding paper these solutions were extensively verified at the local level. In order to study them globally across their phase diagrams, complete non-linear Stokes data (and corresponding connection formulae) are still needed -- all of which are obtained herein. This involves a careful study of (anti-) eigenvalue tunneling across the complete multi-sheeted structure of their associated spectral-curves, and how the result descends from multi-cut smooth-curves to single-cut singular-curves -- all of which are extensively checked via large-order analysis and matrix-integral computations.
